title: Stock Tips
subtitle: ISA, tax, charts & trading how-tos
intro: Practical stock investing tips by category. Tap a title for details.
disclaimer: General information for 2026 only — not tax or investment advice. Confirm your situation with your broker or a tax professional.

type-analysis.label: My type analysis
type-analysis.desc: Investor style, risk, horizon & allocation quizzes

isa-what-is.title: What is an ISA (Individual Savings Account)?
paragraphs: An ISA lets you hold deposits, funds, stocks, and bonds in one account with tax benefits on net income (interest, dividends, and trading gains combined).
Unlike a regular brokerage account, gains and losses are netted, with tax-free limits and a 9.9% flat rate on excess.
You typically must keep the account for a 3-year term to keep full benefits.
tips: Open a dedicated ISA at your bank or broker.
isa-what-is.figureCaption: ISA flow: contribute → invest → tax benefits

isa-yearly-limit.title: What are the ISA annual tax-free limits?
paragraphs: Limits apply to net income (profits minus losses in the account).
General: up to KRW 2M tax-free per year. Worker/farmer/senior types: up to KRW 4M if eligible.
Excess is taxed at 9.9% (separate taxation).
tips: See the ISA table on the tax guide page.
isa-yearly-limit.figureCaption: Annual tax-free limits by ISA type

isa-early-withdrawal.title: What if I withdraw before the 3-year maturity?
paragraphs: Early withdrawal or closure may cancel tax benefits or require repayment of prior benefits.
You can usually withdraw before maturity, but tax treatment becomes unfavorable.
Use early withdrawal only when necessary; staying until maturity is often better.
tips: Check NTS and broker notices for your tax year.
isa-early-withdrawal.figureCaption: Tax downside of early withdrawal before maturity

isa-vs-regular.title: ISA vs regular brokerage account?
paragraphs: Regular account: domestic listed stock gains are generally tax-free (non-major shareholder); dividends withheld at 15.4%.
ISA: nets all product gains in the account; tax-free limit + 9.9% on excess.
Foreign stocks, bonds, and funds inside ISA can be netted together.
tips: Domestic stocks only may be fine in a regular account.

isa-overflow-tax.title: Tax rate above the ISA tax-free limit?
paragraphs: Excess net income is taxed at 9.9% (9% income + 0.9% local).
ISA income is excluded from comprehensive financial income tax — a key benefit.
tips: Often lower than comprehensive rates up to 45%.

isa-comprehensive-tax-exclusion.title: Is ISA income included in comprehensive financial tax?
paragraphs: ISA net income (tax-free and 9.9% portions) is excluded from the KRW 20M financial income threshold.
Useful if regular account interest/dividends approach the limit.
tips: Track regular and ISA income separately.
isa-comprehensive-tax-exclusion.figureCaption: ISA income excluded from comprehensive financial tax

isa-eligibility-types.title: General, worker, and senior ISA types?
paragraphs: General: no income test, KRW 2M tax-free.
Worker/farmer: income requirements, KRW 4M tax-free.
Senior: age 65+, KRW 4M tax-free.
tips: Your broker confirms eligibility at signup.
isa-eligibility-types.figureCaption: ISA types: eligibility and tax-free limits

isa-contribution-limit.title: Annual ISA contribution limit?
paragraphs: Contribution limits are separate from tax-free income limits.
Per-person annual cap is set by regulation (often around KRW 20M), all ISAs combined.
Over-contribution is not allowed.
tips: Limits may change with tax law updates.

isa-maturity-options.title: Options after 3-year ISA maturity?
paragraphs: Convert to pension: possible extra tax benefits on pension withdrawals.
Close and withdraw: keep prior benefits and cash out.
Extension: may be available under product rules.
tips: Compare pension conversion vs cash-out terms.
isa-maturity-options.figureCaption: At maturity: cash out, pension, or extend

isa-loss-offset.title: How are ISA gains and losses netted?
paragraphs: All products in the same ISA are netted together.
Example: +KRW 1M on A and -KRW 300k on B → KRW 700k net for the tax-free limit.
If losses exceed gains, net income may be zero or negative for that year.
tips: Losses offset only within the same ISA and year.
isa-loss-offset.figureCaption: Netting gains and losses within ISA

tax-domestic-capital-gains.title: Tax on domestic stock trading profits?
paragraphs: Non-major shareholders: gains on KOSPI/KOSDAQ listed shares are generally tax-free.
Major shareholders face separate capital gains tax (roughly 22–27.5%).
tips: Unlisted/KONEX may have different rules.
tax-domestic-capital-gains.figureCaption: Domestic stock gains: generally 0% for retail investors

tax-dividend-154.title: Why 15.4% withholding on dividends?
paragraphs: Domestic dividends: 14% income + 1.4% local = 15.4% withheld at source.
If total financial income exceeds KRW 20M/year, comprehensive filing may apply.
tips: Ex-dates and pay dates vary by company.

tax-foreign-gains.title: Tax on foreign stock gains (e.g. US)?
paragraphs: Foreign stock gains are taxable in Korea (around 22% plus local surcharges).
KRW 2.5M basic deduction; typically report in May comprehensive income tax.
tips: Consider foreign tax credit for US withholding.
tax-foreign-gains.figureCaption: Foreign stock capital gains tax summary

tax-foreign-dividend.title: Tax on foreign dividends?
paragraphs: Withheld locally (e.g. US 15–30%); additional tax may apply in Korea.
Report as financial income in May filing.
tips: See foreign dividend table on tax guide.
tax-foreign-dividend.figureCaption: Foreign dividend: local withhold → KR filing

tax-financial-comprehensive.title: Comprehensive financial income tax (KRW 20M)?
paragraphs: If interest + dividends (excluding some items) exceed KRW 20M/year, excess is taxed at progressive rates (6–45%).
ISA net income is excluded from this total.
tips: Important for high-dividend portfolios.

tax-filing-schedule.title: When do I file taxes?
paragraphs: Foreign gains/dividends and comprehensive financial income: usually May comprehensive filing.
Tax-free domestic listed gains: no separate filing.
tips: Use HomeTax or a tax preparer.

tax-securities-transaction.title: What is securities transaction tax?
paragraphs: On domestic stock sales, roughly 0.18–0.23% of sale amount is deducted.
Applies on sell, not buy.
tips: Include fees and tax for realistic P/L.

charts-trendline.title: How to draw trend lines?
paragraphs: Uptrend: line connecting higher lows. Downtrend: line connecting lower highs.
Use at least 2–3 touch points. Break may signal trend change — not a sole signal.
tips: Check index charts on market analysis.

charts-support-resistance.title: Support and resistance?
paragraphs: Support: price level where declines often pause or bounce.
Resistance: level where rallies often stall.
Confirm breaks with volume when possible.
tips: Round numbers and past highs/lows matter psychologically.

charts-rsi.title: How to read RSI?
paragraphs: RSI 0–100; often 70+ overbought, 30- oversold.
Compare with market-wide RSI in app analysis.
Strong trends can stay overbought/oversold for long periods.
tips: RSI divergence is an advanced signal.

charts-macd.title: What does MACD show?
paragraphs: MACD shows momentum from short vs long moving averages.
Signal crossovers and zero-line crosses are references — it lags price.
tips: Compare with market analysis MACD text.

charts-moving-average.title: Moving averages (MA)?
paragraphs: 20/60/120-day lines show short to medium trend.
Golden/death crosses are references; many false signals in sideways markets.
tips: Longer periods = slower but smoother.

charts-volume.title: Why volume matters?
paragraphs: Rising price + rising volume: stronger participation. Price up, volume down: weaker follow-through.
Check volume on breakouts.
tips: Volume drop after spike may mean short-term exhaustion.

charts-vix.title: What is VIX?
paragraphs: VIX estimates expected volatility from S&P 500 options — a fear gauge.
Higher VIX = more market anxiety.
Useful global sentiment reference for KR investors too.
tips: See VIX section in market analysis.
charts-vix.figureCaption: VIX: market fear and volatility gauge

charts-caution.title: Trade on charts alone?
paragraphs: Charts show past price patterns, not guaranteed future.
Combine with fundamentals, news, position sizing, and diversification.
Define stop-loss and sizing rules in advance.
tips: Use technical + fundamental + risk management together.
charts-caution.figureCaption: Do not trade on charts alone

trading-average-cost.title: Average cost (cost basis)?
paragraphs: Average purchase price across multiple buys.
App recalculates from trades and corporate actions.
Additional buys change your average.
tips: Align fee/tax treatment with your broker display.

trading-pnl.title: Unrealized vs realized P/L?
paragraphs: Unrealized: (current price − cost) × shares for holdings still owned.
Realized: locked in when you sell.
Dashboard totals depend on definitions used.
tips: Tax generally applies to realized gains (with domestic listed exceptions).

trading-market-vs-limit.title: Market vs limit orders?
paragraphs: Market: fill quickly at current prices; slippage possible.
Limit: only at your price or better; may not fill.
Limits often help in volatile or thin markets.
tips: App records trades; place orders in your broker app.

trading-dividend-ex-date.title: Ex-dividend and record dates?
paragraphs: Ex-date: day dividend rights separate from price; must hold day before.
Rights adjustments for splits/bonus issues.
Buying just before ex-date rarely nets free money after price drop and tax.
tips: Record dividends in Trades & Dividends.
trading-dividend-ex-date.figureCaption: Hold before ex-date; price adjusts after

trading-corporate-actions.title: Splits, mergers & corporate actions?
paragraphs: Split: more shares, lower price per share.
Mergers/spin-offs adjust quantity and cost basis.
Log actions in the app to keep holdings correct.
tips: Reconcile broker notices with app records.

trading-quantity.title: How is share quantity calculated?
paragraphs: Buys − sells + corporate action adjustments = current quantity.
Fractional shares depend on broker support (common for US).
tips: Zero shares removes from portfolio but keeps history.

accounts-brokerage.title: Regular brokerage account?
paragraphs: Standard account for stocks, ETFs, bonds.
Domestic gains often tax-free; dividends 15.4% withheld.
Often used alongside ISA/pension.
tips: You can hold ISA + regular at one broker.

accounts-isa-role.title: Role of an ISA account?
paragraphs: Tax benefits: netting, tax-free limit, 9.9% excess.
3-year term, contribution caps, early exit penalties.
Consider for long-term diversified investing with tax savings.
tips: See Stock Tips ISA category and tax guide together.

accounts-pension.title: Pension savings vs stock account?
paragraphs: Pension/IRP focus on retirement and contribution credits (up to ~13.2% on contributions).
Often fund/deposit heavy; direct stock rules vary by product.
May link to ISA maturity pension conversion.
tips: Check annual limits on tax guide.

accounts-cma.title: What is a CMA?
paragraphs: Cash management account linked to brokerage for idle cash and short-term products.
Used for parking funds before investing.
Separate from stock trading mechanics.
tips: Match app cash balance with broker CMA.

portfolio-diversification.title: Why diversify?
paragraphs: Concentration in one stock/sector increases specific risk.
Spread across names, sectors, countries (KR/US), and asset types.
Use allocation and simulation in the app.
tips: No perfect diversification — match your risk tolerance.

portfolio-rebalancing.title: What is rebalancing?
paragraphs: Adjust holdings back to target weights (e.g. 70% stocks / 30% cash).
Sell overweight, add underweight on a schedule.
Too frequent rebalancing increases costs.
tips: Quarterly or semi-annual reviews are common.
portfolio-rebalancing.figureCaption: Portfolio weights before and after rebalancing

portfolio-cash-ratio.title: How much cash to hold?
paragraphs: Some cash buffers downturns and enables future buys.
100% invested vs cash is personal — situation and comfort differ.
Check cash vs total assets on dashboard.
tips: Keep emergency living funds outside brokerage.

portfolio-long-term.title: Long-term vs short-term trading?
paragraphs: Long-term: growth, dividends, compounding; lower turnover and stress.
Short-term: more fees, tax, and time; needs discipline.
Beginners often start small, long-term, diversified.
tips: Define horizon and goal (retirement, lump sum, etc.) first.

analysis-investor-type.title: Full investor type quiz (10 steps)
paragraphs: Ten questions on horizon, loss tolerance, experience, income, emergency fund, knowledge, crisis behavior, return expectations, diversification, and goals.
Classifies you into one of 10 types from ultra conservative to ultra aggressive, with asset mix, KR/US weights, and stock style suggestions.
You can apply results directly to portfolio target weights.
tips: About 3–5 minutes
Tap “Apply to portfolio targets” after finishing.

analysis-risk-check.title: Quick risk tolerance quiz (5 questions)
paragraphs: Five questions on loss tolerance, crisis response, return expectations, emergency fund, and diversification preference.
Useful to gauge how much volatility you can handle when markets fall.
Best as a light check before or alongside the full quiz.
tips: About 1–2 minutes
Use together with the full investor type quiz.

analysis-horizon-goal.title: Horizon & goal check (5 questions)
paragraphs: Five questions on time horizon, purpose, experience, income stability, and knowledge.
Helps clarify whether your money is short-term or long-term and what you are investing for.
If horizon and goals do not match stocks, lowering equity weight is OK.
tips: About 1–2 minutes
Keep living expenses and emergency cash outside brokerage.

analysis-allocation-style.title: Allocation style quiz (5 questions)
paragraphs: Five questions on diversification, return expectations, loss tolerance, purpose, and horizon.
Points toward cash, bonds, ETFs, or individual stocks in your mix.
Compare with the full quiz and adjust simulation targets in the app.
tips: About 1–2 minutes
Review alongside app simulation target weights.
